chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Suleyman al-Farra', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding the fasting one who applies kohl, he said: There is no problem with it; it is neither food nor drink.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Suleyman al-Farra', from someone else, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: Does applying kohl break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that applying kohl does not invalidate the fast, as the Imam emphasizes its classification as neither food nor drink, distinguishing it from substances that provide nourishment. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that minor external applications do not disrupt the spiritual state of fasting, provided they do not reach the stomach through the primary digestive channels. The transmission chain highlights the reliability of early narrators like Sulayman al-Farra’ in establishing this practical legal nuance for daily worship.
